chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed lust from the women of the Clan of Hashim and placed it in their men, and similarly He did with their Shias; and indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed lust from the men of the Clan of Umayya and placed it in their women, and similarly He did with their adherents.

key_terms.بَنُو أُمَيَّة: The Clan of Umayya, the rival lineage
key_terms.بَنُو هَاشِم: The Clan of Hashim, the lineage of the Prophet and the Imams

ai.seo_question: How did Allah distinguish the spiritual and physical characteristics of the clans of Hashim and Umayya?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights a metaphysical distinction in spiritual temperament (khuluq) between the Ahl al-Bayt and the Umayyads, a concept central to Shia theology regarding the purity of the Imams. It suggests that the 'shahwah' (desire/passion) in Banu Hashim is refined and directed towards divine love and leadership, whereas in Banu Umayya it is often associated with worldly ambition, a trait mirrored in their respective followers (shi'ah). This distinction underscores the theological argument for the unique spiritual status of the Prophet's household and their true followers.
